title: A section of an etale algebra splits off a factor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $R\to S$ a ring map with $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $s:S\to R$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras. Then there is an idempotent $e\in S$ with $s(e)=1$ and $\ker s=(1-e)S$. Consequently $S\cong R\times(1-e)S$ as $R$-algebras, $s$ corresponding to the first projection, and $s$ induces an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $S_e\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ from the localization $S_e=S[1/e]$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), (5)$\Rightarrow$(2), first paragraph: 'the surjective ring map $A'/IA'\to A/I$ is etale by Algebra, Lemma 00U7 (lemma-map-between-etale) and then we get the desired idempotent by Algebra, Lemma 00U8 (lemma-surjective-flat-finitely-presented)' (literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex); used without comment in the proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): '$B'/IB'=A/I\times C$'

proof.text: *$s$ is surjective and $\operatorname{Spec}s$ is etale.* Let $\iota:R\to S$ be the structure map. Since $s$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, $s\circ\iota=\mathrm{id}_R$; hence $s$ is surjective. On spectra, $\operatorname{Spec}\iota\circ\operatorname{Spec}s=\operatorname{Spec}(s\circ\iota)=\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$, so $\operatorname{Spec}s:\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ is a morphism between the two $\operatorname{Spec}R$-schemes $\mathrm{id}:\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\iota:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ commuting with the structure morphisms. The first is an open immersion, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1); the second is etale by hypothesis [def-weil-etale-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3) (with $f=\operatorname{Spec}s$, $g=\operatorname{Spec}\iota$, $g\circ f=\mathrm{id}$), $\operatorname{Spec}s$ is etale. (Stacks: 'the surjective ring map $A'/IA'\to A/I$ is etale by Algebra, Lemma 00U7'.)

proof.text: *$\ker s$ is generated by an idempotent.* Put $I=\ker s\subseteq S$. By step 1, $s:S\to R$ is a surjective ring map with $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ etale, so by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-etale-kernel-idempotent-fg] (applied with $A=S$, $B=R$, $\varphi=s$) $I^2=I$ and $I$ is finitely generated. By [lem-weil-pbc-fg-idempotent-ideal-idempotent-generator] (1) there is an idempotent $e'\in S$ with $I=e'S$. (Stacks: 'then we get the desired idempotent by Algebra, Lemma 00U8'; 00U8, first proof: $I$ finitely generated, $I/I^2=0$, conclude by Lemma 00EH.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 00U8 (lemma-surjective-flat-finitely-presented), first proof, with Lemma Tag 00EH (lemma-ideal-is-squared-union-connected) (1); invoked in literature/stacks-project/more-algebra.tex, proof of Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), (5)$\Rightarrow$(2), first paragraph

proof.text: *The idempotent $e$.* Put $e=1-e'$. Then $e^2=1-2e'+e'^2=1-e'=e$, so $e$ is idempotent, and $1-e=e'$. As $e'\in I=\ker s$, $s(e)=s(1)-s(e')=1$. And $\ker s=e'S=(1-e)S$. This is the first assertion.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): 'let $g\in B'$ map to $(1,0)\in A/I\times C$'; the computation is written out by the agent

proof.text: *$S\cong R\times(1-e)S$.* The ideal $(1-e)S$ is a commutative ring under the operations of $S$ with unit $1-e$ (as $(1-e)\cdot(1-e)x=(1-e)x$), and an $R$-algebra via $r\mapsto(1-e)\iota(r)$. Define $\Phi:S\to R\times(1-e)S$, $\Phi(x)=(s(x),(1-e)x)$. It is additive, $\Phi(1)=(1,1-e)$, multiplicative because $(1-e)xy=(1-e)^2xy=((1-e)x)((1-e)y)$, and $R$-linear because $\Phi(\iota(r))=(r,(1-e)\iota(r))$; so $\Phi$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras whose first component is $s$. Injective: if $s(x)=0$ and $(1-e)x=0$, then $x\in\ker s=(1-e)S$, say $x=(1-e)y$, so $x=(1-e)^2y=(1-e)x=0$. Surjective: given $(r,(1-e)y)$, put $x=e\,\iota(r)+(1-e)y$; then $s(x)=s(e)r+s(1-e)s(y)=r$ (step 3: $s(e)=1$, $s(1-e)=0$) and $(1-e)x=(1-e)e\,\iota(r)+(1-e)^2y=(1-e)y$. Hence $\Phi$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $S\cong R\times(1-e)S$ under which $s$ is the first projection. (Mathlib has the equivalent form $S\cong S/(1-e)S\times S/eS$, `AlgEquiv.prodQuotientOfIsIdempotentElem`, RingTheory/Idempotents.lean:475.)

proof.text: *$S_e\cong R$ via $s$.* $s$ is a surjective ring map with $\ker s=(1-e)S$ and $e$ idempotent (steps 1, 3), so by [lem-weil-pbc-fg-idempotent-ideal-idempotent-generator] (2) the map $S_e=S[1/e]\to R$, $x/e^n\mapsto s(x)s(e)^{-n}=s(x)$, induced by $s$ (defined since $s(e)=1$), is an isomorphism; it is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras because $s$ is one and $\iota(r)/1\mapsto s(\iota(r))=r$. (Stacks 00U8: 'there exist an idempotent $e\in R$ such that $S=R_e$'.)

lean.statement: theorem exists_idempotent_splitting_of_algHom {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.Etale R S] (s : S →ₐ[R] R) : ∃ (e : S) (he : IsIdempotentElem e), s e = 1 ∧ RingHom.ker s.toRingHom = Ideal.span {1 - e} ∧ (∃ (_ : Algebra R he.one_sub.Corner), (∀ r : R, (algebraMap R he.one_sub.Corner r).1 = (1 - e) * algebraMap R S r) ∧ ∃ Φ : S ≃ₐ[R] R × he.one_sub.Corner, ∀ x : S, (Φ x).1 = s x) ∧ (∃ ψ : Localization.Away e ≃ₐ[R] R, ∀ x : S, ψ (algebraMap S (Localization.Away e) x) = s x)
